reviews.title: Bought this before the RAMPOCALYPSE!! Beautiful, sleek performer despite being DDR4
reviews.comment: It's an impressive performer. First off, the build quality feels solid, with a sleek heat spreader design that not only looks great but also helps with thermal performance during intense sessions. The overclocking capabilities are noteworthy; I was able to push the RAM to 3600MHz, and it maintained stability throughout. (I've owned this set for about 8 months, no crashes at all whatsoever) In terms of performance, this kit delivers a noticeable boost in multitasking and gaming scenarios, particularly when paired with a high-performance CPU. The 3600MHz speed is excellent for both gaming and content creation, providing a smooth and responsive experience. I mainly use Adobe After Effects, which requires a good bit of RAM, and this set does deliver such phenomenal and NOTICEABLE performance compared to 16GB, in which I have upgraded from. Coming from a Ryzen AM4 system, I've never really had any compatibility issues. The DDR4 fit perfectly fine! No stress whatsoever :) Overall, the TEAMGROUP T-CREATE Expert DDR4 kit is a fantastic choice for enthusiasts wanting to maximize their system's potential. It strikes a good balance between performance, reliability, and aesthetic appeal. Highly recommended!
reviews.author: Dexter Jon

reviews.title: Great memory
reviews.comment: This memory is actually quite good and I'm pleasantly impressed! I was able to achieve a very rock-solid stable overclock of 3800MT/s @  CL18 with 1.350 V. It's a decent bit above the advertised XMP speeds of 3600, and helps to bridge the gap of the slightly higher CAS latency. I've had zero issues with it and having the extra headroom sure is nice when dealing with memory-hungry applications. I was amazed that in one such case, the application I was using which didn't usually even try to max out my 32GB kit, immediately utilized 38GB+ of this kit under the same configuration and operating conditions. So the application was previously holding itself back due to my hardware limitation and I didn't even know it If you need the headroom (which I confess, most don't on average), then this is an excellent and cost-effective way to get it! Oh, did I mention that it's sleek, low-profile, with relatively subtle branding? It's easily forgettable in my otherwise flashy PC lol, but that's not a bad thing. Highly recommended Update: just bought another 64gb due to that one RAM hungry program now maxing out my 64gb. My particular setup was not perfectly stable when overclocked to 3800MT/s with the same settings, but it's running very stable with the stock XMP profile. Still quite happy with this RAM, I feel like I got away with something getting it for so cheap!
